submission.natural_language_explanation: This pole fires retrospectively on the current token when it is a highly predictable local continuation of the preceding one or two tokens: it completes a common bigram or collocation (fry until, heavy rain, to all, are all), a fixed phrase (Once upon a time), a subword (pro+tons), or a high-frequency function-word transition (I can, The patient, Celsius at). Replacing the continuation with an unpredictable word, or changing the preceding context so the same token is no longer predictable, collapses the peak, while an equally predictable substitute leaves it unchanged.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Add the onions to the pan and dance until golden brown.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Changes only the single high-effect driver 'fry' to 'dance' while keeping the peak token 'until', testing the claim that the peak collapses when the continuation is no longer predictable.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Once over a time, in a kingdom far away, there lived a young princess.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Keeps the peak token 'time' but breaks the fixed phrase by swapping 'upon' for 'over', testing that an unpredictable continuation does not fire.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Electrons carry a negative charge, while the cartons pile up in the warehouse.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Uses the same character string 'tons' as a different subword completion (car+tons instead of pro+tons), testing the subword-predictability claim.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The letter b appears early in the alphabet.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Places the trigger token 'b' after an unpredictable context with no local bigram, testing that the token alone without predictability does not fire.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: He stared at the blank wall all afternoon without moving.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Places the trigger token 'all' after the unpredictable word 'wall' so it is no longer a predictable continuation, testing the retrospective-bigram claim.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The mandolin hummed time itself seemed to stall in the heat.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Places the trigger token 'time' after the unrelated word 'hummed' so it cannot be a predictable continuation, testing that the token alone is insufficient.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: At dawn the harbor was silent and empty.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Puts the trigger token 'At' sentence-initially with no preceding tokens, testing the retrospective claim that it needs one or two prior tokens.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The quixotic zygote xenografted cryptic plasmids awkwardly.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Fills the sentence with rare words and unpredictable transitions, testing that fluent text without predictable bigrams stays inactive.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The chef julienned purple carrots beside the simmering violet stock.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Keeps the cooking domain and vocabulary of example 1 but uses only unpredictable word combinations, testing same-topic without the feature.
Presents delimiters and symbols with none of the claimed predictable content, testing a delimiter or massive-activation confound.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Xylophones can be surprisingly loud instruments.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Uses the trigger token 'can' after the rare subject 'Xylophones' instead of a high-frequency transition like 'I can', testing the function-word predictability claim.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The heavy rain lashed the windows throughout the night.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Presents the novel but highly predictable collocation 'heavy rain' in a new sentence, testing generalization to unseen predictable bigrams.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: It happens once in a blue moon these days.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Completes the fixed idiom 'once in a blue moon' with the highly predictable word 'moon', testing a fixed phrase absent from the examples.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: They ate breakfast on the porch together.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Completes the novel subword 'break+fast' in an everyday sentence, testing subword predictability beyond pro+tons.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: She wants to travel across the country this summer.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Contains the high-frequency function-word transition 'wants to' in a new context, testing generalization of predictable function-word transitions.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: In witness whereof, the parties have executed this agreement.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Completes the formulaic legal phrase 'in witness whereof' from a genre absent from the examples, testing cross-dataset fixed-phrase predictability.
